# 10-Week Statistics Study Roadmap

A 6-hour weekly plan works well here: 3 focused study blocks, 1 review block, and 1 practice/test block each week. Since probability and hypothesis testing are the hardest areas, they get extra time and repeated revisits.

## Weekly Topic Breakdown

| Week | Focus | Hours | Main Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Descriptive statistics + data types | 6 | Summarize data with mean, median, spread, and graphs |
| 2 | Probability foundations | 6 | Compute basic probabilities and interpret events |
| 3 | Conditional probability + counting rules | 6 | Solve multi-step probability problems confidently |
| 4 | Random variables + distributions | 6 | Understand expected value and common distributions |
| 5 | Sampling + Central Limit Theorem | 6 | Connect samples to population behavior |
| 6 | Confidence intervals | 6 | Build and interpret intervals correctly |
| 7 | Hypothesis testing basics | 6 | Set up null/alternative hypotheses and make decisions |
| 8 | Hypothesis testing applications | 6 | Run tests for means/proportions and read p-values |
| 9 | Correlation + regression | 6 | Analyze relationships and interpret fitted lines |
| 10 | Full review + mock exam | 6 | Identify weak spots and complete timed practice |

## Progress-Tracking Chart Idea

Use a simple line chart or bar chart with these 3 series:

- **Planned hours**: always 6 per week
- **Completed hours**: actual hours studied each week
- **Mastery score**: 0–100 rating after each week’s quiz

Chart setup:
- X-axis: Week 1 to Week 10
- Left Y-axis: Hours
- Right Y-axis: Mastery score
- Add a goal line at **80% mastery**
- Color code:
  - Blue = planned hours
  - Green = completed hours
  - Orange = mastery score

This makes progress easy to see at a glance and highlights where probability and hypothesis testing need extra review.

## Sample Milestone Table

| Milestone | Target Week | Success Check |
|---|---:|---|
| Descriptive stats mastered | 1 | Can summarize a dataset without notes |
| Probability basics solid | 3 | Can solve basic and conditional probability questions |
| Distribution concepts clear | 4 | Can match scenarios to the right distribution |
| Confidence intervals understood | 6 | Can explain what an interval means in context |
| Hypothesis testing ready | 7 | Can set up hypotheses and choose a test |
| Test interpretation accurate | 8 | Can interpret p-values and conclusions correctly |
| Regression basics complete | 9 | Can read slope, intercept, and correlation |
| Exam readiness reached | 10 | Score 80%+ on a timed practice exam |

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Download Plan] https://www.google.com/search?q=10-week+statistics+study+plan+template
Action: [Button: Practice Problems] https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability

- Khan Academy Statistics & Probability: https://www.khanacademy.org/math/statistics-probability
- OpenStax Introductory Statistics: https://openstax.org/details/books/introductory-statistics
- NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook: https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/
